name: The Continuous Close
title: The Continuous Close
answer: Continuous close is the practice of keeping the books close to current, so reconciliations, accruals, and reporting are updated continuously rather than only at month end. It sits in financial reporting and synthesis, where the goal is a reliable, auditable view of the ledger at any point in time. It covers transaction matching, account reconciliation, journal entry preparation, variance analysis, and the handoff to internal and external reporting. It does not remove the need for a controlled period close, but it changes when and how the work happens.

sections.body: Continuous close is the practice of keeping the books close to current, so reconciliations, accruals, and reporting are updated continuously rather than only at month end. It sits in financial reporting and synthesis, where the goal is a reliable, auditable view of the ledger at any point in time. It covers transaction matching, account reconciliation, journal entry preparation, variance analysis, and the handoff to internal and external reporting. It does not remove the need for a controlled period close, but it changes when and how the work happens.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The continuous close runs on a connected data layer that pulls from ERP, subledgers, banks, payment processors, and other source systems. It needs reliable identifiers, consistent charts of accounts, and a warehouse or lakehouse that can hold both detailed transactions and summarized balances. Automation services, reconciliation engines, and reporting tools sit on top, often with workflow and approval queues. Controls, audit trails, and access management are part of the infrastructure, not add-ons.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by matching transactions as they arrive, flagging exceptions, and routing them to the right owner. Rules handle known patterns, while models help with fuzzy matching, anomaly detection, and coding suggestions. Accountants review exceptions, approve adjustments, and sign off on reconciliations, so the close becomes a steady stream of small decisions. The period end then becomes a review and lock step rather than a rush to gather and fix everything.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The continuous close depends on clear ownership of data, models, and controls. Every automated match, adjustment, and journal entry needs a traceable source, a timestamp, and a reviewer where material. Provenance matters because auditors and regulators will ask how a balance was produced and whether the process is repeatable. Access rights, segregation of duties, and change management protect the ledger from silent errors or misuse. Privacy and retention rules apply to the underlying transaction data, especially across borders.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more frequent, more automated, and more explainable close processes. Expect tighter integration between ERP, reconciliation, and reporting, with AI assisting on exceptions rather than replacing judgment. Adoption will vary by company size, regulatory burden, and data quality, so many organizations will run hybrid cycles for some time. The likely outcome is a close that is always nearly done, with period end reserved for review, disclosure, and sign-off.
